about: The files a BranchKit app release publishes, and which of them an install or an update uses.
branchkit-cli embeds this file (release_assets.go): `app download` picks this machine's file from it.
The release assembler reads the same file, so the names it writes are the names the updater looks for.
A release is the tag `tag_prefix` + version (version X.Y.Z) on GitHub `repository`.
In `name`, {version} is X.Y.Z and {arch} is the spelling `arch` maps this machine's Go GOARCH to.
`use` says what consumes the file: `install` (a person's first install) and/or `update` (the updater).
Each OS has exactly one `update` file. Linux packages are left to the package manager that owns the files.
`checksums` lists every other file in sha256sum's text format (`<sha256 hex>  <name>`, sorted by name, LF).
The release is published immutable, so GitHub attests it: no signature file is an asset.
The updater reads that attestation from GitHub's attestations API by the checksums file's digest.

artifacts.name: BranchKit-{version}-macos-{arch}.dmg
artifacts.about: Disk image holding BranchKit.app, for a first install.

artifacts.name: BranchKit-{version}-macos-{arch}.zip
artifacts.about: BranchKit.app zipped with `ditto -c -k --keepParent`, which keeps its signature and extended attributes; the updater swaps it in place.

artifacts.name: BranchKit-{version}-windows-{arch}.zip
artifacts.about: The install folder and install.ps1, for a first install and for an update.

artifacts.name: branchkit_{version}_{arch}.deb
artifacts.about: Debian and Ubuntu package; apt updates it.

artifacts.name: BranchKit-{version}-{arch}.AppImage
artifacts.about: AppImage for any distribution; no package manager owns it, so the updater replaces it.
